style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare-transliteration in amp with Strong's carried in notes (matching the ch.1 pilot); em-dashes used sparingly. Transliterations are ASCII-normalized (lowercase, diacritics dropped) relative to the lexicon's spellings.
chapterNote: Chapter 11 opens the great antithetical collection of Solomon, where nearly every line sets the righteous against the wicked and tracks where each one's road ends. The chapter begins where commerce begins -- at the scales (v.1) -- and insists that the LORD Himself watches the merchant's weights, then widens outward to show how a single just or wicked life ripples through the whole city (vv.10-11). Its drumbeat is reversal and return: riches cannot ransom from wrath (v.4), the trap a man sets springs back on him (vv.5-8), what is generously scattered comes back enlarged (vv.24-25), and the harvest a man reaps is the seed he sowed (vv.18-19, 30-31). The fear of the LORD is no longer named outright, but His scales and His delight hold the whole chapter together.

1.text: A rigged scale is detestable to the LORD, but an honest weight is His delight.
1.amp: A false balance [mirmah -- deceit, fraud worked into the very scales] is an abomination [to'evah -- a thing the LORD finds loathsome] to the LORD, but a full and honest weight [even shalem -- literally a 'complete stone,' the merchant's stone neither shaved nor padded] is His delight [ratzon -- His favor and good pleasure].
1.notes: even shalem (H68 + H8003) is literally a 'whole stone' -- ancient weights were stones, and a shaved or doctored one cheated the buyer; mirmah (H4820) is calculated fraud. The LORD's interest in to'evah (H8441) and ratzon (H7522) at the marketplace shows His holiness reaches into ledgers and weights, not only altars (cf. Deut 25:13-16; Prov 16:11).

2.text: When arrogance arrives, disgrace comes in close behind it; but wisdom keeps company with the humble.
2.amp: When pride [zadon -- insolent, swaggering arrogance] comes, then comes shame [qalon -- public disgrace, dishonor]; but with the lowly [tsana -- those who walk modestly, who carry themselves humbly] is wisdom [chokmah].
2.notes: the Hebrew plays on arrival -- pride 'comes in,' and qalon (H7036) follows it through the same door; zadon (H2087) is willful, in-your-face arrogance. tsana (H6800) is a rare verb for walking humbly (cf. Mic 6:8); chokmah lodges not with the self-important but with the modest who can still be taught. Also tagged: chokmah (H2451).

3.text: The integrity of the upright is their guide, but the crookedness of the treacherous is their ruin.
3.amp: The integrity [tummah -- wholeness, an undivided honesty] of the upright [yashar -- the straight, the level] guides [nachah -- leads, conducts] them, but the perverseness [selef -- the twist, the distortion] of the treacherous [bagad -- the faithless, the betrayers] destroys [shadad -- devastates, lays waste] them.
3.notes: tummah (H8538) is integrity as wholeness -- a life with no hidden seam -- and it functions as a road-guide (nachah, H5148); selef (H5558) is the inner twist that does the opposite work. bagad (H898), to deal treacherously, names the same covenant-betrayers as 2:22. A man is led or wrecked by what he is on the inside. Also tagged: yashar (H3477), shadad (H7703).

4.text: Wealth is worth nothing on the day of wrath, but righteousness rescues from death.
4.amp: Riches [hon -- accumulated wealth, substance] do not profit [yaal -- avail, do any good] in the day [yom] of wrath [evrah -- overflowing fury], but righteousness [tsedaqah] delivers [natsal -- snatches away] from death [mavet].
4.notes: evrah (H5678) is wrath that overflows its banks -- divine judgment that no fortune can buy off (cf. Zeph 1:18; Ezek 7:19). natsal (H5337), to snatch from danger, recurs across this chapter; tsedaqah (H6666), not wealth, is the only currency that ransoms a man at the last. The same pairing of wealth-against-death anchors v.28. Also tagged: hon (H1952), yaal (H3276), yom (H3117), mavet (H4194).

5.text: The righteousness of the blameless smooths his road straight, but the wicked is brought down by his own wickedness.
5.amp: The righteousness [tsedaqah] of the blameless [tamim -- whole, without defect] makes his way [derek] straight [yashar -- levels it, sets it right], but the wicked [rasha] falls [naphal -- topples, collapses] by his own wickedness [risha].
5.notes: tamim (H8549) is wholeness without a hidden crack (cf. 2:21); yashar as a verb (H3474) is to make a road level and straight. The wicked needs no outside executioner -- his own risha (H7564) is the weight that fells him (naphal, H5307). The verse turns on the contrast between a leveled path and a self-caused collapse. Also tagged: tsedaqah (H6666), derek (H1870), rasha (H7563).

6.text: The righteousness of the upright sets them free, but the treacherous are caught in their own craving.
6.amp: The righteousness [tsedaqah] of the upright [yashar] delivers [natsal -- rescues] them, but the treacherous [bagad -- the faithless] are taken [lakad -- captured, snared] in their own greedy craving [havvah -- engulfing desire that becomes their destruction].
6.notes: natsal (H5337) again -- righteousness rescues (cf. vv.4, 8) -- while havvah (H1942) is a double-edged word meaning both 'craving' and 'calamity,' so the desire and the disaster are one. lakad (H3920) is the hunter's word: the betrayers are trapped in the very appetite they would not master. Also tagged: tsedaqah (H6666), yashar (H3477), bagad (H898).

7.text: When a wicked man dies, his hope dies with him, and all that he expected from his strength comes to nothing.
7.amp: When a wicked [rasha] man [adam] dies [mavet], his expectation [tikvah -- the hope he stretched toward, like a taut cord] perishes [abad -- is lost, comes to ruin], and the hope [tochelet] of his power perishes [abad] as well.
7.notes: tikvah (H8615) comes from a root for a stretched cord -- hope as a line cast forward into the future; at death that cord is cut. abad (H6) is to perish utterly, repeated for force. Whatever the wicked banked on -- his strength, his schemes -- has no reach past the grave (cf. Ps 49:17; Luke 12:20). tochelet (H8431) is the second word for hope. The phrase behind 'his power' is tagged aven (H205), usually 'iniquity' -- the KJV reads 'the hope of unjust men' -- but the same consonants can be read as on, 'strength,' the sense followed here; either way, what the wicked leaned on dies with him. Also tagged: rasha (H7563), adam (H120), mavet (H4194).

8.text: The righteous is pulled out of trouble, and the wicked walks in to take his place.
8.amp: The righteous [tsaddiq] is drawn out [chalats -- hauled out, freed] of trouble [tsarah -- the tight, pressing distress], and the wicked [rasha] comes [bo -- enters] in his place.
8.notes: chalats (H2502) is to be pulled free, the opposite of being pinned; tsarah (H6869) is constricting distress (cf. 1:27). The verse pictures a strange exchange -- the trap empties of the righteous and closes on the wicked who took his stead -- a pattern Scripture shows literally with Haman and Mordecai (Esth 7:10). Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563), bo (H935).

9.text: With his mouth the godless man wrecks his neighbor, but through knowledge the righteous are rescued.
9.amp: With his mouth [peh -- his speech] the godless [chaneph -- the profane, the hypocrite] destroys [shachath -- ruins, corrupts] his neighbor [rea -- his fellow, his friend], but through knowledge [daat] the righteous [tsaddiq] are delivered [chalats -- drawn out, set free].
9.notes: chaneph (H2611) is the man hollowed of true reverence whose words do quiet damage; shachath (H7843) is to ruin or spoil. The rescue-verb chalats (H2502) carries over from v.8 -- there from trouble, here from the slanderer's tongue -- and the deliverer is daat (H1847), the knowledge that sees through the godless man's speech. Also tagged: peh (H6310), rea (H7453), tsaddiq (H6662).

10.text: When the righteous prosper, the city is glad; and when the wicked perish, there is a shout of joy.
10.amp: When it goes well [tov -- with goodness, prosperity] with the righteous [tsaddiq], the city [qiryah] rejoices [alats -- exults, leaps for joy]; and when the wicked [rasha] perish [abad], there is a ringing shout [rinnah -- a glad cry, a public shout].
10.notes: the chapter widens from the individual to the public square: a righteous man's flourishing is civic good news, and rinnah (H7440) is the communal shout of relief when a tyrant falls. abad (H6) echoes v.7 -- the wicked perishes both privately and to the city's open joy. Righteousness is never a merely private virtue. Also tagged: tov (H2898), tsaddiq (H6662), qiryah (H7151), alats (H5970), rasha (H7563).

11.text: By the blessing of the upright a city is lifted high, but by the mouth of the wicked it is torn to the ground.
11.amp: By the blessing [berakah -- the spoken good, the benediction] of the upright [yashar] the city [qeret] is exalted [rum -- raised up, lifted high], but by the mouth [peh] of the wicked [rasha] it is torn down [haras -- demolished, pulled to the ground].
11.notes: the pair to v.10 names the mechanism: a city rises (rum, H7311) on the berakah (H1293) of its upright citizens and is demolished (haras, H2040) by the peh of its wicked ones -- the same mouth that wrecked a neighbor in v.9 now levels a town. Public life is built or broken by the character of its speakers. Also tagged: yashar (H3477), qeret (H7176, the poetic word for city), peh (H6310), rasha (H7563).

12.text: Whoever belittles his neighbor has no sense, but a person of understanding holds his tongue.
12.amp: He who is void [chaser -- lacking, destitute] of sense [leb -- heart, here the seat of judgment] despises [buz -- holds in contempt, sneers at] his neighbor [rea], but a man [ish] of understanding [tebunah] keeps silent [charash -- holds his peace, stays quiet].
12.notes: the Hebrew of 'void of sense' is literally 'lacking heart' (chaser leb, H2638 + H3820), since the leb was the seat of thought, not just feeling. buz (H936) is contemptuous sneering; charash (H2790) means to be silent (also to plow or engrave). Wisdom is shown here as much by the mouth kept shut as by the words spoken. Also tagged: rea (H7453), ish (H376), tebunah (H8394).

13.text: A gossip goes about exposing secrets, but a trustworthy spirit keeps a confidence covered.
13.amp: A talebearer [rakhil -- a peddler of gossip, going from house to house] reveals [galah -- uncovers, lays bare] secrets [sod -- confidential counsel, intimate trust], but he of a faithful [aman -- trustworthy, reliable] spirit [ruach] conceals [kasah -- covers over] the matter [dabar].
13.notes: rakhil (H7400) is a slanderer pictured as a traveling peddler (the KJV's 'he that walketh' captures the going-about); sod (H5475) is the intimate council shared in trust. galah (H1540), to uncover, is the very word for exile -- to betray a confidence is to expose what should stay covered (kasah, H3680). A faithful ruach (H7307) guards what it is given. Also tagged: aman (H539), dabar (H1697).

14.text: For lack of wise direction a people collapses, but in a wealth of counselors there is deliverance.
14.amp: Where there is no wise guidance [tachbulot -- skillful steering, the ropes that turn a ship] the people [am] fall [naphal -- collapse, go down], but in the multitude [rob] of counselors [yoatz -- advisers, those who plan] there is safety [teshuah -- deliverance, victory].
14.notes: tachbulot (H8458) comes from a root for ship's ropes -- the steering-lines of a nation (cf. 1:5); without that wise handling, the am (H5971) capsizes (naphal, H5307). teshuah (H8668) is deliverance that amounts to victory; the safeguard is not one genius but a chorus of yoatz (H3289). Humility to seek counsel is itself wisdom. Also tagged: rob (H7230).

15.text: He who guarantees a stranger's debt is sure to suffer for it, but the one who refuses to shake on such pledges stays safe.
15.amp: He who is surety [arab -- pledges himself, becomes the guarantor] for a stranger [zar -- an outsider, someone he scarcely knows] will surely come to harm [ra -- suffer evil, be broken by it], but he who hates [sane] the striking of hands in pledge [taqa -- the handclap that sealed a guarantee] is secure [batach -- safe, confident].
15.notes: arab (H6148) is to put oneself up as collateral; the deal was sealed by 'striking hands' (taqa, H8628), the ancient handshake of guarantee. To co-sign for a zar (H2114), an unknown outsider, is to gamble one's own ruin; the man who declines such pledges rests in batach (H982), settled security (cf. 6:1-5; 22:26-27). Also tagged: ra (H7451), sane (H8130).

16.text: A gracious woman holds onto honor, just as ruthless men hold onto riches.
16.amp: A gracious [chen -- favor, charm, kindness] woman [ishshah] retains [tamak -- takes firm hold of, keeps fast] honor [kavod -- weight, dignity, glory], and ruthless [arits -- violent, terrifying] men retain [tamak] riches [osher].
16.notes: the verse sets a quiet contrast through a repeated verb: tamak (H8551), to grip and hold fast, governs both lines -- the woman of chen (H2580) lays hold of kavod (H3519, honor, literally 'weight'), while violent men (arits, H6184) only grip osher (wealth). What each truly secures reveals what each truly is; honor outlasts the riches held by force. Also tagged: ishshah (H802), osher (H6239).

17.text: A kind man does good to his own soul, but a cruel man brings trouble on his own flesh.
17.amp: The merciful [chesed -- one marked by steadfast, loyal love] man [ish] does good [gamal -- deals out benefit, recompenses] to his own soul [nephesh], but the cruel [akzari -- pitiless, merciless] man troubles [akar -- brings ruin upon, stirs up trouble for] his own flesh [sheer -- his own body, his kin].
17.notes: chesed (H2617) is covenant-loyal kindness -- here the man who embodies it; gamal (H1580) is to deal out, for good or ill. The mercy or cruelty a man shows comes home to his own nephesh (H5315) and sheer (H7607, flesh or near kin): kindness nourishes the self, cruelty corrodes it (akar, H5916). A man's character is the first thing his character touches. Also tagged: ish (H376), akzari (H394).

18.text: The wicked man earns wages that betray him, but the one who sows righteousness reaps a wage that holds.
18.amp: The wicked [rasha] works [asah -- makes, produces] a deceitful [sheqer -- false, treacherous] wage [peullah -- work and its pay], but to him who sows [zara -- scatters seed] righteousness [tsedaqah] comes a sure [emet -- true, reliable, lasting] reward [seker -- wages, hire].
18.notes: sheqer (H8267) is falsehood -- the wicked man's earnings lie to him, promising what they cannot keep; emet (H571) is the firm, trustworthy opposite. The sowing-and-reaping image (zara, H2232) frames the moral life as agriculture: what a man plants, he will harvest (cf. Gal 6:7-8; Hos 10:12). One wage evaporates, the other endures. Also tagged: rasha (H7563), asah (H6213), peullah (H6468), tsedaqah (H6666), seker (H7938).

19.text: As righteousness leads on to life, so the one who chases evil chases it to his own death.
19.amp: As righteousness [tsedaqah] tends toward life [chayyim], so he who pursues [radaph -- chases hard, hunts down] evil [ra] pursues it to his own death [mavet].
19.notes: radaph (H7291) is to chase with full effort, even to persecute -- and the irony is exact: the man hunts evil and so hunts down his own mavet (H4194). The two roads of v.18's harvest are here named by their destinations, life and death, the book's master either/or (cf. Deut 30:19; Prov 12:28). Also tagged: tsedaqah (H6666), chayyim (H2416), ra (H7451).

20.text: Those with twisted hearts are detestable to the LORD, but those whose way is whole are His delight.
20.amp: Those of a perverse [iqqesh -- crooked, bent out of true] heart [leb] are an abomination [to'evah] to the LORD, but those who are blameless [tamim -- whole, sound] in their way [derek] are His delight [ratzon].
20.notes: the verse circles back to v.1's vocabulary of to'evah (H8441) and ratzon (H7522), now applied not to scales but to the heart: a leb (H3820) that is iqqesh (H6141), bent off-line, is loathsome to God, while a tamim (H8549) walk is His pleasure. What the LORD weighs is finally not the merchant's stone but the man's heart. Also tagged: derek (H1870).

21.text: Be assured of this -- the wicked will not go unpunished, but the children of the righteous will be brought through safe.
21.amp: Hand to hand [yad le-yad -- an idiom of certainty, like a handshake on a promise], the wicked [ra] will not go unpunished [naqah -- be held innocent, go free of guilt], but the offspring [zera -- the seed, the descendants] of the righteous [tsaddiq] will be delivered [malat -- escape, be brought safely out].
21.notes: yad le-yad (H3027), 'hand joined to hand,' is a Hebrew idiom for what is settled and sure -- as good as sealed. naqah (H5352) is to be acquitted; the wicked will not be. By contrast the zera (H2233) of the righteous -- their very seed -- finds malat (H4422), escape and rescue, an echo of covenant blessing reaching to children's children (cf. Exod 20:6; Ps 112:2). Also tagged: ra (H7451), tsaddiq (H6662).

22.text: Like a gold ring in a pig's snout is a beautiful woman who has thrown discretion away.
22.amp: As a ring [nezem -- a nose-ring or earring of jewelry] of gold [zahav] in a swine's snout [aph -- the pig's nose], so is a beautiful [yapheh] woman [ishshah] who turns aside [sur -- departs, removes herself] from discretion [taam -- good taste, sound judgment, discernment].
22.notes: nezem (H5141) was fine ornament; set in a pig's aph (H639) -- an unclean animal rooting in filth -- it is grotesque waste. taam (H2940) means literally 'taste,' and so discernment, the sense to tell good from foul; beauty without it (sur, H5493, having departed from it) is a treasure squandered in the mud. The proverb prizes judgment over looks. Also tagged: zahav (H2091), yapheh (H3303), ishshah (H802).

23.text: The longing of the righteous can end only in good; the expectation of the wicked ends in wrath.
23.amp: The desire [taavah -- longing, the deep want of the heart] of the righteous [tsaddiq] is only good [tov], but the expectation [tikvah -- the hope stretched toward the future] of the wicked [rasha] is wrath [evrah -- overflowing fury].
23.notes: taavah (H8378) is desire that can run to lust, but in the righteous it bends only toward tov (H2896). tikvah (H8615) recalls v.7 -- the wicked man's cord of hope -- and its terminus here is evrah (H5678), the same overflowing wrath of v.4. Two hearts reach for the future; what each reaches into is decided by what each loves. Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), rasha (H7563).

24.text: One man scatters freely and grows richer still; another hoards what he ought to give, and only comes to want.
24.amp: There is one who scatters [pazar -- disperses, gives liberally] and yet increases [yasaph -- gains more, adds to himself]; and there is one who withholds [chasak -- holds back, spares] more than is right [yosher -- what is fitting, upright], yet it leads only to poverty [machsor -- want, need, lack].
24.notes: the central paradox of the chapter's generosity cluster: pazar (H6340), to scatter as a farmer flings seed, ends in yasaph (H3254), increase; while ungenerous chasak (H2820), clutching past what is fitting (yosher, H3476), ends in machsor (H4270), want. The kingdom's economy runs backward to the miser's instinct (cf. 2 Cor 9:6; Luke 6:38).

25.text: A generous soul will be made rich, and whoever refreshes others will himself be refreshed.
25.amp: The soul [nephesh] of blessing [berakah -- the liberal, open-handed one] will be made fat [dashen -- made prosperous, enriched, anointed], and he who waters [ravah -- saturates, gives others their fill] will himself be watered [yarah -- be soaked, given drink] as well.
25.notes: literally 'a soul of blessing' (nephesh berakah, H5315 + H1293) -- the open-handed person; dashen (H1878) is to be made fat, the image of flourishing and abundance. The harvest metaphor turns to irrigation: the one who pours out water to others is himself rained upon (ravah, H7301), a self-returning kindness (cf. v.24; Matt 5:7). yarah (H3384) is elsewhere 'to throw' or 'to teach,' but the form here has long been rendered 'shall be watered' (so the KJV) -- rain-language, the sense followed above.

26.text: The people curse the man who hoards his grain, but blessing crowns the head of the one who sells it.
26.amp: He who withholds [mana -- holds back, keeps from others] grain [bar -- threshed grain, wheat], the people [leom -- the populace, the nation] will curse [naqab -- denounce, pronounce against] him, but blessing [berakah] will rest on the head [rosh] of him who sells [shabar -- sells out grain, supplies it] it.
26.notes: in a famine the man who hoards bar (H1250) to drive up the price earns the people's curse (naqab, H5344, to denounce or pierce with words), while the one who releases it to market is crowned with berakah (H1293) on his rosh (H7218). Generosity and commerce are not opposed; the proverb blesses the trader who keeps grain moving to the hungry. Also tagged: mana (H4513), leom (H3816), shabar (H7666).

27.text: Whoever searches hard for good wins favor, but whoever hunts for harm -- harm will find him.
27.amp: He who diligently seeks [shachar -- seeks early and earnestly, as at dawn] good [tov] obtains [baqash -- seeks out and secures] favor [ratzon -- goodwill, acceptance], but he who searches after [darash -- inquires for, pursues] evil [ra], it will come [bo] to him.
27.notes: shachar (H7836) is to seek at daybreak, urgently and first (cf. 1:28) -- the man who rises early for tov finds ratzon (H7522), the same favor that is the LORD's delight in v.1. But darash (H1875), to seek out evil, is answered in kind: what a man hunts for comes home to roost. Pursuit boomerangs, for good or for ill. Also tagged: tov (H2896), baqash (H1245), ra (H7451), bo (H935).

28.text: Whoever leans on his riches will fall, but the righteous will thrive like green new growth.
28.amp: He who trusts [batach -- relies on, rests his confidence in] his riches [osher] will fall [naphal -- topple, collapse], but the righteous [tsaddiq] will flourish [parach -- blossom, sprout, break into bloom] like a green leaf [aleh -- fresh foliage].
28.notes: batach (H982) is the verb of confident trust -- but riches (osher) are a foundation that gives way (naphal, H5307, as in v.5). The righteous instead parach (H6524), bursts into leaf like a watered tree (cf. Ps 1:3; 92:12-14; Jer 17:7-8). The verse exposes where a man's true security lies. Also tagged: osher (H6239), tsaddiq (H6662), aleh (H5929).

29.text: Whoever brings trouble on his own house inherits nothing but wind, and the fool ends up a servant to the wise of heart.
29.amp: He who troubles [akar -- brings ruin on, stirs up disorder in] his own house [bayit -- household, family] will inherit [nachal -- take as his inheritance] the wind [ruach -- breath, emptiness], and the fool [evil -- the morally senseless one] becomes servant [eved -- slave] to the wise [chakam -- skillful, discerning] of heart [leb].
29.notes: akar (H5916), the troubling verb of v.17, here ruins a whole bayit (H1004); the man's inheritance (nachal, H5157) turns out to be ruach (H7307) -- mere wind, nothing he can hold. The reversal is sharp: the evil (H191), the senseless fool, ends up serving the chakam (H2450), the one with skill of heart -- folly forfeits even its own estate. Also tagged: eved (H5650), leb (H3820).

30.text: The fruit of a righteous life is a tree of life, and the one who wins souls is wise.
30.amp: The fruit [peri] of the righteous [tsaddiq] is a tree [ets] of life [chayyim], and he who wins [laqach -- takes, draws in, gathers] souls [nephesh] is wise [chakam].
30.notes: peri (H6529) yields not just fruit but a whole ets chayyim (H6086 + H2416), a tree of life -- the imagery of Eden restored through a righteous life (cf. 3:18; Gen 2:9). laqach (H3947), to take or gather, gives the line its missionary edge ('he that taketh souls'): wisdom does not only save the self but draws others toward life (cf. Dan 12:3; Jas 5:20). Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), nephesh (H5315), chakam (H2450).

31.text: If the righteous receive their due here on earth, how much more the wicked man and the sinner!
31.amp: Behold, the righteous [tsaddiq] will be recompensed [shalam -- repaid, made complete, requited] in the earth [eretz]; how much more the wicked [rasha] and the sinner [chote -- the one who misses the mark, the offender]!
31.notes: shalam (H7999) is to repay and so to bring to completion -- if even the tsaddiq is requited within this life, the lesser-to-greater argument lands with weight on the rasha and chote (H2398). The Septuagint of this verse is quoted in 1 Peter 4:18, pressed toward final judgment: if the righteous are barely brought through, where will the ungodly stand? Also tagged: tsaddiq (H6662), eretz (H776), rasha (H7563).
